project.one_sentence: Middle-school students' ability to notice, describe and use variability in data when drawing conclusions.

literature.verdict: No jangle risk; one related-but-distinct construct kept separate.

constructs.name: Informal inferential reasoning
constructs.definition: Drawing generalisations beyond the data without formal procedures.
constructs.action: Sharpen distinction: ours stops at describing and using spread.

constructs.name: Variation (statistics)
constructs.definition: Spread of a distribution as a statistic, not a reasoning skill.

waypoints.label: Ignores variability
waypoints.definition: Treats single values as the whole story; differences between cases are not noticed.

waypoints.label: Notices variability
waypoints.definition: Points out that values differ but does not describe how much or why.

waypoints.label: Describes variability
waypoints.definition: Describes spread with a range, clusters or informal measures.

waypoints.label: Uses variability
waypoints.definition: Uses spread to judge how confident a comparison or conclusion can be.

expert_review.issues: W3 mixes informal and formal measures.
expert_review.revisions: Say 'informal or formal measures of spread'.

resolution.W2: Round 1 mixed W2/W3; added 'no quantity or pattern named' to W2.

bank.text: Two classes' plant heights: which class grew more evenly? Explain.
